title: HMAC accumulation buffer grows to full message size before hardware flush
description: crypto2dev_hmac accumulates all wc_HmacUpdate data into a heap-allocated buffer (doubling growth), flushed to hardware only at wc_HmacFinal. No upper bound on buffer size. A caller computing HMAC over large data (e.g., 1GB file integrity) will XMALLOC the full input before the first hardware op. No documented limit, no error until MEMORY_E from the allocator. For TLS record MACs (max ~16KB) this is fine. For any caller using crypto2dev HMAC for bulk data integrity, it is a silent OOM risk. The public API (wc_HmacUpdate) gives no indication that the entire data is buffered.
